title: Se impersonal: debates sobre religión y Estado

sections.content: Impersonal se lets you describe what a country did — strengthened the Church, signed a concordat, resolved a dispute — without naming a specific actor, which fits a narrative about institutional shifts more than individual decisions. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En lugar de reducirse la influencia de la Iglesia católica, se la fortaleció deliberadamente como pilar del orden social.
items.english: Instead of the Catholic Church's influence being reduced, it was deliberately strengthened as a pillar of the social order.

items.spanish: Se llegó a declarar, en la constitución de 1869, que solo los católicos podían ser ciudadanos ecuatorianos.
items.english: It even came to be declared, in the 1869 constitution, that only Catholics could be Ecuadorian citizens.

items.spanish: No se resolvió esta disputa hasta la revolución liberal de 1895, liderada por Eloy Alfaro.
items.english: This dispute wasn't resolved until the 1895 liberal revolution, led by Eloy Alfaro.

items.spanish: Durante casi un siglo, no se separaron completamente en Colombia los asuntos religiosos de los asuntos del Estado.
items.english: For nearly a century, religious matters and matters of state were not completely separated in Colombia.

sections.content: Se fortaleció / se llegó a declarar / no se resolvió / no se separaron: the impersonal se works with singular or plural verbs depending on whether what follows is a singular idea (se resolvió esta disputa) or a plural noun phrase (se separaron los asuntos), so check what the sentence is really describing before conjugating.
